sections.content: How many people stayed in Milton Keynes after gaining qualifications?

Milton Keynes is a large town in the South East. Milton Keynes also has a university.

Milton Keynes has medium levels of deprivation.

Overall, Milton Keynes ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 8,010 state-school pupils from Milton Keynes who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 2,820 (35%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 2,355 (29%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Milton Keynes to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Milton Keynes' pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Milton Keynes in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Milton Keynes move to?

Of Milton Keynes's graduates, 990 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 200 of those graduates (20%) were living fairly locally, in the Milton Keynes travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Milton Keynes's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 685 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 275 of those qualified non-graduates (40%) were living fairly locally, in the Milton Keynes travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Milton Keynes' GCSE cohort:

  • 735 graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 405 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was the East Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 29% of graduates and 24% of qualified non-graduates living in Milton Keynes had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 2,520 graduates and 2,150 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Milton Keynes. This is compared with the 2,820 graduates and 2,355 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 71% of the graduates had also lived in Milton Keynes as GCSE pupils, while 29% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Milton Keynes in 2018 to 2019, 76% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 24% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
